OPEN
This is open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation.
Find the optimal constant $c>0$ such that the following holds. 
For all sufficiently large $N$, if $A\sqcup B=\{1,\ldots,2N\}$ is a partition into two equal parts, so that $\lvert A\rvert=\lvert B\rvert=N$, then there is some $x$ such that the number of solutions to $a-b=x$ with $a\in A$ and $b\in B$ is at least $cN$. 
#36: [Er55][Er56][Er61][Er92c]
number theory | 
additive combinatorics
The minimum overlap problem. The example (with $N$ even) $A=\{N/2+1,\ldots,3N/2\}$ shows that $c\leq 1/2$ (indeed, Erdős initially conjectured that $c=1/2$). The lower bound of $c\geq 1/4$ is trivial, and Scherk improved this to $1-1/\sqrt{2}=0.29\cdots$. The current records are\[0.379005 < c < 0.380876,\]the lower bound due to White [Wh22] and the upper bound due to the TTT-Discover LLM [YKLBMWKCZGS26], improving slightly on earlier bounds due to AlphaEvolve [GGTW25] and Haugland [Ha16].
This is discussed in problem C17 of Guy's collection [Gu04].
Additional thanks to: Terence Tao
